summary: Every named attack fails, and the acceptance-criteria accounting is exact at the bytes rather than merely plausible. acceptanceCriteriaStanding marks AC-1, AC-3 and AC-4 NOT discharged and AC-2 satisfied, and each supporting fact reproduces: EVIDENCE really is at claim-register claims/30, status CANDIDATE, bound to evidence.v10; evidence.v15 really is at 28dc3c1a; and the commissioned validator really is REJECT at 1 blocker per blueprint §1.1. The rowQuoted status is faithful to live file 08. The disposition forecloses the coordinator-authority axis in the strongest available form -- 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording' -- which forecloses my own verdict being read as the owner act. One advisory: P-002-3's state-class bound compresses D-002 State's two named DR-124 classes into a phrase that reads as one class with two adjectives, and its sibling disposition for DR-004 states the same bound correctly.

advisoriesList.observation: The bound reads 'Rebuildable or journaled operational metadata (DR-124 / D-002 State)'. Adopted D-002's State clause names two distinct classes: 'local, non-authoritative only — rebuildable cache/index and operational metadata classes (DR-124)'. DR-124 defines 'Rebuildable cache/index' and 'Operational metadata' as separate classes with different Plan/Run consequences and custody rules -- the former 'discarded/rebuilt; provenance and corruption tests prove no authority or hidden input', the latter 'Excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly' admits it.
advisoriesList.whyItMatters: Dropping 'cache/index' after 'Rebuildable' turns two class names into one class name with two adjectives, so the phrase reads as an assertion that operational metadata is rebuildable. That is the collapse route-b.DR-005.v1 was rejected for. A designer reading this bound cannot tell which class's Plan/Run rule governs the surface being permitted.
advisoriesList.whyItIsNotABlocker: Both classes are in fact permitted for the preview by D-002 State, so the compression admits nothing that is forbidden and excludes nothing that is required. The governing source is cited by name, so a reader can resolve it. The accompanying exclusions -- 'Not evidence custody. Not replay-as-authority. Not a sealed Run.' -- correctly rule out the authoritative-evidence class.
advisoriesList.theRemedyIsInTheCompanionDocument: The DR-004 disposition drafted alongside this one states the identical bound correctly at P-004-3: 'Rebuildable cache/index or journaled operational metadata.' Copying that phrasing closes this. The two dispositions currently disagree with each other about how to name the same pair of classes.
advisoriesList.alsoObserved: 'journaled' is not DR-124 vocabulary for either class; D-002 State does not use it either. It appears in both dispositions, so it is a deliberate authoring choice rather than a slip, but it is not traceable to the cited sources.

verdictNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. This is a careful draft and the axis that would matter most — pretending the applied evidence.v15 head discharges an acceptance criterion — is foreclosed criterion by criterion, with every supporting fact reproducing at the bytes including the exact claims/30 pointer. It also forecloses the subtler risk that my own ACCEPT is mistaken for the owner act. The single advisory is a naming compression: D-002 State permits two DR-124 classes and this bound renders them as one class with two adjectives. It admits nothing forbidden, which is why it is not a blocker, but it is the collapse a sibling disposition was rejected for, and the correct wording already exists in the DR-004 draft filed with it.
